data.body:
Fixes bug Bfc43dae5b9: ddflow_wait via MCP with timeout=1800 sent no response or progress for 1800s and the client aborted it (MCP tool idle timeout). The tool should emit progress notifications while waiting, or cap its default/max timeout below the client idle limit; shell 'ddflow wait --timeout 570' works.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-Bfc43dae5b9 --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed Bfc43dae5b9 --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug Bfc43dae5b9: MCP ddflow_wait gives no progress; client aborts at 1800s idle

chunk_findings.detail: The manual gives two mutually exclusive startup orders. Line 11 says "Call `ddflow_brief` FIRST, before anything else," while line 25 says that if several agents or subagents are present, "call `ddflow_identify` first." In the multi-agent case, following line 11 causes the exact failure the manual itself describes at lines 28-30: identity is derived from the shared worktree, the agents merge into a single identity, `ddflow_brief` answers with someone else's task, and a review gate can compare the agent against itself. An agent in that environment may claim or edit the wrong item.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/manual.md:11 and :25

chunk_findings.detail: The manual instructs that `ddflow_brief` "replaces reading this project's rule and lesson files — do not read those instead," but `ddflow_brief` is described as returning decisions that govern the files about to be touched and lessons ranked for the current task. The manual never restates the global advisory r-ddflow-self-assessment (assess ddflow at the end of every agent run, phase, and before context compaction). An agent that obeys the manual's prohibition on reading the rule files has no remaining source for that required self-assessment and will omit it. This violates the advisory.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/manual.md:13-15 [r-ddflow-self-assessment]

chunk_findings.detail: The compact text “One of several agents: `ddflow_identify` first, or `as_agent` on every call” makes `ddflow_identify` first an acceptable option on the stateless `2026-07-28` revision. On that revision there is no initialize connection, so `ddflow_identify` persists nothing; the old instructions explicitly said to name yourself on every call via `as_agent` or `_meta`. Given multiple agents in one worktree on that revision, an agent calls `ddflow_identify` once and stops; unlabeled later calls are derived from the working tree, identities merge, `ddflow_brief` can answer with someone else’s task, and a review gate can compare the agent against itself and pass.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/mcp_instructions.md:44

chunk_findings.detail: The unconditional loop “`ddflow_merge`, `ddflow_complete`” removes the PR integration branch. In a project with `[flow].integration = "pr"`, `ddflow_merge` opens the pull request, parks the item IN REVIEW, and releases the lease; the original contract said “do not wait and do not `ddflow_complete` it — take the next item.” The new charter tells that agent to call `ddflow_complete` on a parked item, producing a refusal/confusing loop exactly in the PR-flow case.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/mcp_instructions.md:44

chunk_findings.detail: The "byte cap" is checked with `len(text)`, which counts Unicode code points, not UTF-8 bytes. The previous `mcp_instructions` pipeline line contained `" implement ·"` (U+00B7), so non-ASCII characters can make `len(text) <= 1500` while `len(text.encode()) > 1500`; the same issue is in the unadopted assertion at line 50 and the SessionStart assertion at line 75. Thus the cap this test is meant to enforce is not actually enforced.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_charter_contract.py:44

chunk_findings.detail: After setting `gates.task_pipeline` to `implement,unit_tests,merge`, the test locates the `Gates:` line and only asserts that `rubber_duck` is absent. It no longer asserts that the configured gates appear, so a broken `_instructions` output such as `Gates: research · critic` passes both assertions. The test named `test_the_pipeline_shown_is_the_project_s_own` would fail to catch a regression that renders a different pipeline.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_instructions.py:66

chunk_findings.detail: The pointer assertion is `assert "topic=manual" in _instructions(repo) or "manual" in _instructions(repo)`. Since `"manual"` is a substring of `"topic=manual"`, the second clause makes the first redundant and allows any mention of the word "manual" to satisfy the check. An instructions text like `"This is not a manual; call ddflow_help."` passes even though it never names the `manual` topic, so the test does not prove the charter points at the manual.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_charter_contract.py:57

chunk_findings.detail: The manual asserts “A plain `ddflow_review` of a gate with a recorded review is a full re-review”, but the same parenthetical states `full=true` is needed when `[review].delta_default` is on—meaning a plain `ddflow_review` is not a full re-review in that configuration. Under `[review].delta_default = true`, an agent following the broad statement will call plain `ddflow_review` expecting the whole diff; the tool actually performs a delta review only (full requires `full=true`), so the full diff is never re-reviewed and a gate can pass with unreviewed changes. The sentence must be qualified: plain is full only when `delta_default` is off; when it is on, plain is delta and `full=true` is required for a full review.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/manual.md:88-90

chunk_findings.detail: The cap is measured with `len(text.encode())`, which counts UTF-8 bytes, while the project cap is specified in characters (`<=1.5K chars`, `CHARTER_MAX_CHARS`). Given an adopted charter of 1500 characters containing one non-ASCII character such as `—` (3 UTF-8 bytes), line 45 reports `1502 bytes > 1500` and fails even though the character cap is met. The same `.encode()` byte measurement is reused at lines 53 and 85, so valid non-ASCII framing would be incorrectly rejected.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_charter_contract.py:45

chunk_findings.detail: The SessionStart contract in the intent includes “where to fetch more” (`ddflow_recall`/`ddflow_help`), but this test only asserts that `"claim"`, `"operator"`, `"unavailable"`, and `"ddflow_brief"` appear in `SESSION_START_HEADER + SESSION_START_FOOTER`. A framing such as `"ddflow_brief first. claim before edit. ask the operator. unavailable never passed."` with an empty footer would pass the test even though it omits the fetch-more instruction, so the test does not enforce the contract it is named for.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_charter_contract.py:85

chunk_findings.detail: The new test does not exercise the behavior it is replacing. It calls `_instruction_vars(repo)`, then forcibly overrides `vars_["actionable_companions"] = []` before rendering, so it never verifies how `_instruction_vars` decides that no companion needs action. The removed test `test_a_registered_companion_is_not_listed_as_missing` actually registered `context7` and checked the real served instructions omitted it. Concrete missing input: a repository where `context7` is registered but `_instruction_vars` still returns it in `actionable_companions` — the served instructions would still say “not wired up”, yet this test passes because the hand-set `[]` hides the bug. The regression guard is lost.

chunk_findings.detail: The manual instructs that `ddflow_brief` "replaces reading this project's rule and lesson files — do not read those instead," but `ddflow_brief` is described as returning decisions that govern the files about to be touched and lessons ranked for the current task. The manual never restates the global advisory r-ddflow-self-assessment (assess ddflow at the end of every agent run, phase, and before context compaction). An agent that obeys the manual's prohibition on reading the rule files has no remaining source for that required self-assessment and will omit it. This violates the advisory.

chunk_findings.detail: The compact text “One of several agents: `ddflow_identify` first, or `as_agent` on every call” makes `ddflow_identify` first an acceptable option on the stateless `2026-07-28` revision. On that revision there is no initialize connection, so `ddflow_identify` persists nothing; the old instructions explicitly said to name yourself on every call via `as_agent` or `_meta`. Given multiple agents in one worktree on that revision, an agent calls `ddflow_identify` once and stops; unlabeled later calls are derived from the working tree, identities merge, `ddflow_brief` can answer with someone else’s task, and a review gate can compare the agent against itself and pass.

chunk_findings.detail: The unconditional loop “`ddflow_merge`, `ddflow_complete`” removes the PR integration branch. In a project with `[flow].integration = "pr"`, `ddflow_merge` opens the pull request, parks the item IN REVIEW, and releases the lease; the original contract said “do not wait and do not `ddflow_complete` it — take the next item.” The new charter tells that agent to call `ddflow_complete` on a parked item, producing a refusal/confusing loop exactly in the PR-flow case.

chunk_findings.detail: The "byte cap" is checked with `len(text)`, which counts Unicode code points, not UTF-8 bytes. The previous `mcp_instructions` pipeline line contained `" implement ·"` (U+00B7), so non-ASCII characters can make `len(text) <= 1500` while `len(text.encode()) > 1500`; the same issue is in the unadopted assertion at line 50 and the SessionStart assertion at line 75. Thus the cap this test is meant to enforce is not actually enforced.

The test named `test_the_pipeline_shown_is_the_project_s_own` would fail to catch a regression that renders a different pipeline.

chunk_findings.detail: The pointer assertion is `assert "topic=manual" in _instructions(repo) or "manual" in _instructions(repo)`. Since `"manual"` is a substring of `"topic=manual"`, the second clause makes the first redundant and allows any mention of the word "manual" to satisfy the check. An instructions text like `"This is not a manual; call ddflow_help."` passes even though it never names the `manual` topic, so the test does not prove the charter points at the manual.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_charter_contract.py:57

chunk_findings.detail: The first step still says “Call `ddflow_brief` FIRST, before anything else” while in the same rewritten sentence says, for one of several agents/subagents, “name yourself first.” Those are two different first actions, and the absolute “before anything else” is not made conditional. In a shared worktree, an agent that follows the leading absolute instruction and calls `ddflow_brief` with no identity first is the same failure mode previously described: identity is derived from the shared worktree, so the agent can receive another agent’s task and later review comparisons can bind to the wrong work. chunk_findings.detail: The manual asserts “A plain `ddflow_review` of a gate with a recorded review is a full re-review”, but the same parenthetical states `full=true` is needed when `[review].delta_default` is on—meaning a plain `ddflow_review` is not a full re-review in that configuration. Under `[review].delta_default = true`, an agent following the broad statement will call plain `ddflow_review` expecting the whole diff; the tool actually performs a delta review only (full requires `full=true`), so the full diff is never re-reviewed and a gate can pass with unreviewed changes. The sentence must be qualified: plain is full only when `delta_default` is off; when it is on, plain is delta and `full=true` is required for a full review.

chunk_findings.detail: The manual authorizes an agent to resolve an un-made project flow choice without the operator: “ask the operator, or choose what suits the project with `ddflow_flow_choose` and a reason.” The contract this change is supposed to preserve is “ask the operator.” An agent that follows the “or choose” branch on a project-level branching-model/release-line decision can unilaterally set operator-owned policy with `ddflow_flow_choose`, bypassing the required operator decision.

A freshly initialised project with every setup notice on therefore emits an injection well over the advertised 1500 characters (for the all-ASCII setup-sentence output, 2208 bytes is 2208 chars). A future edit that follows this comment can still pass the fresh-init test while producing output ~700 chars over the stated budget, so the cap claimed in the file is false for an actual agent-facing surface.

chunk_findings.detail: The manual instructs the agent to "Call `ddflow_brief` FIRST, before anything else" at line 11, then at line 25 instructs an agent in a multi-agent/subagent context to "call `ddflow_identify` first." These two first-step orders are mutually exclusive and the manual never states which one has precedence. In a multi-agent workspace, an agent that obeys line 11 calls `ddflow_brief` before `ddflow_identify`, contrary to the multi-agent-specific order the section itself says is required to avoid merging identities, receiving another agent's task, and a review gate comparing the agent against itself.

chunk_findings.detail: For `gate_gaps`, the new line says “Gates with no tool behind them: …; record `unavailable`, never imply a tool ran.” But `gate_gaps` contains gates the agent is expected to perform directly — the removed text explicitly said “Several of those are judgement you do directly — that is fine and expected.” Concrete input: a repository whose pipeline has `standards` but no codeguide-mcp installed, so `standards` appears in `gate_gaps`. Following the new instruction, the agent records `standards` as `unavailable` even after doing the manual standards review. That produces a false “could not run” result and discards the actual direct judgement/evidence. `unavailable` is for a tool or reviewer that could not run, not for a gate that has no external tool behind it.

chunk_findings.detail: `drift_notes(repo)` always emits “`ddflow adopt --agents claude` refreshes them” for every non-current state, including `edited`. The module’s own contract says a hand edit is kept. Given a repo with a hand-edited `.claude/agents/ddflow-researcher.md`, `states()` returns `{".claude/agents/ddflow-researcher.md": "edited"}`, and `drift_notes()` then falsely tells the user that the command refreshes that file, even though the command is supposed to leave hand edits untouched.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leanagents.py:drift_notes

chunk_findings.detail: The generated implementer role includes `mcp__ddflow__ddflow_wait` in its `tools:` list. This conflicts with [r-lock-cycle-selfheal], which says agents never poll-wait or hold while waiting. If an implementer encounters a dependency or block, it can call that tool and hold, exactly what the rule says ddflow must heal by adding needs edges instead. The role definition should not grant `ddflow_wait` to a non-operator agent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-implementer.md:4

chunk_findings.detail: The implementer template defines the role’s full contract but never instructs the agent to perform the end-of-run / phase / pre-compaction ddflow self-assessment required by [r-ddflow-self-assessment]. An agent launched from this file can finish without filing any discovered ddflow bugs, misbehavior, or missing features because no assessment step is present, and the body does not point to a hook that enforces it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-implementer.md:8-15

chunk_findings.detail: Both `description` values are unquoted YAML plain scalars that contain `: ` (colon followed by a space): "Read-only ddflow research: gathers…" and "Independent ddflow reviewer: reads…". YAML forbids colon+space inside a plain scalar, so a standard frontmatter parser throws `mapping values are not allowed here`; Claude Code will fail to load either agent definition.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-researcher.md:3 and ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-reviewer.md:3

chunk_findings.detail: Both roles state "Never edits files" / "You edit no file", but the `tools:` list includes `Bash`. Claude Code's Bash has no read-only mode, so the agent can execute mutating shell commands such as `sed -i 's/TODO/FIXME/g' src/*.py` or `echo > file`; the read-only guarantee is prose only and is not enforced by the agent definition an input that asks for a repo-wide edit can modify files.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-researcher.md:4 and ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-reviewer.md:4

chunk_findings.detail: The test invokes `run_cli(repo, "adopt", "--agents", "cursor")` but discards the exit code and any stderr, then only checks that `.claude/agents` does not exist. Given a broken implementation where `adopt --agents cursor` immediately exits non-zero before writing any files, the assertion still passes, so the test is vacuously true under exactly the failure mode it should distinguish from a successful non-Claude adoption. It should first assert the command succeeded and that the intended cursor files were written before asserting no Claude definitions are produced.

chunk_findings.detail: The `description` value is an unquoted YAML plain scalar containing the sequence `: ` (`... end to end: claim ...`). In YAML, `: ` is a mapping-value indicator and is not allowed inside a plain scalar; standard YAML parsers (PyYAML/js-yaml) will fail with an error such as `mapping values are not allowed here`. This makes the entire frontmatter invalid, so the `ddflow-implementer` agent definition cannot be loaded by `ddflow adopt`/Claude Code.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-implementer.md:3

chunk_findings.detail: The body instructs "Call `ddflow_brief` first" and later refers to `ddflow_research_add`, `ddflow_recall`, `ddflow_help`, and `ddflow_rule_show` without the MCP prefix, but the frontmatter only grants `mcp__ddflow__ddflow_brief`, `mcp__ddflow__ddflow_research_add`, etc. A generated subagent that follows the instruction literally will attempt a tool named `ddflow_brief`, which does not exist in its tool list and is rejected by Claude Code, so the role cannot perform its required first action.

chunk_findings.detail:
`_front` turns a YAML block list into a Python list, so `tools = [t.strip() for t in str(fm["tools"]).split(",")]` is not a valid parser for the generated templates when `tools:` is written as:

```

  - Bash
  - Read

```

The assertion then fails for every role, even though the definition correctly names `ddflow_brief`.

chunk_findings.detail: `drift_notes(repo)` always emits “`ddflow adopt --agents claude` refreshes them” for every non-current state, including `edited`. The module’s own contract says a hand edit is kept. Given a repo with a hand-edited `.claude/agents/ddflow-researcher.md`, `states()` returns `{".claude/agents/ddflow-researcher.md": "edited"}`, and `drift_notes()` then falsely tells the user that the command refreshes that file, even though the command is supposed to leave hand edits untouched.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leanagents.py:drift_notes

chunk_findings.detail: The generated implementer role includes `mcp__ddflow__ddflow_wait` in its `tools:` list. This conflicts with [r-lock-cycle-selfheal], which says agents never poll-wait or hold while waiting. If an implementer encounters a dependency or block, it can call that tool and hold, exactly what the rule says ddflow must heal by adding needs edges instead. The role definition should not grant `ddflow_wait` to a non-operator agent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-implementer.md:4

chunk_findings.detail: The implementer template defines the role’s full contract but never instructs the agent to perform the end-of-run / phase / pre-compaction ddflow self-assessment required by [r-ddflow-self-assessment]. An agent launched from this file can finish without filing any discovered ddflow bugs, misbehavior, or missing features because no assessment step is present, and the body does not point to a hook that enforces it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-implementer.md:8-15

chunk_findings.detail: Both `description` values are unquoted YAML plain scalars that contain `: ` (colon followed by a space): "Read-only ddflow research: gathers…" and "Independent ddflow reviewer: reads…". YAML forbids colon+space inside a plain scalar, so a standard frontmatter parser throws `mapping values are not allowed here`; Claude Code will fail to load either agent definition.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-researcher.md:3 and ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-reviewer.md:3

chunk_findings.detail: Both roles state "Never edits files" / "You edit no file", but the `tools:` list includes `Bash`. Claude Code's Bash has no read-only mode, so the agent can execute mutating shell commands such as `sed -i 's/TODO/FIXME/g' src/*.py` or `echo > file`; the read-only guarantee is prose only and is not enforced by the agent definition an input that asks for a repo-wide edit can modify files.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-researcher.md:4 and ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-reviewer.md:4

chunk_findings.detail: The test invokes `run_cli(repo, "adopt", "--agents", "cursor")` but discards the exit code and any stderr, then only checks that `.claude/agents` does not exist. Given a broken implementation where `adopt --agents cursor` immediately exits non-zero before writing any files, the assertion still passes, so the test is vacuously true under exactly the failure mode it should distinguish from a successful non-Claude adoption. It should first assert the command succeeded and that the intended cursor files were written before asserting no Claude definitions are produced.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lean_agents.py:test_adopt_for_another_agent_writes_no_claude_definitions

chunk_findings.detail: The added line only instructs the implementer to file ddflow defects “At the end of the run.” [r-ddflow-self-assessment] also requires the assessment at the end of every phase and before context compaction. Given an implementer run that compacts context before the run ends, an ddflow bug visible only in the discarded context is never filed because the only instruction occurs later, so the new line does not fully answer the role’s self-assessment obligation.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-implementer.md:15

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten `drift_notes()` message is still unconditional for every non-current state: it says `ddflow adopt --agents claude` “rewrites the managed region (a hand edit is saved beside the file).” For a missing definition, e.g. a repo where `.claude/agents/ddflow-researcher.md` does not exist and `states()` reports that path as `missing`, there is no managed region and no hand edit to save; adopt creates a fresh template instead, so the note gives false recovery information for that state.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leanagents.py:100

chunk_findings.detail: The tools line drops `mcp__ddflow__ddflow_research_add` and inserts `mcp__ddflow__ddflow_bug_found`. The description still says the researcher "files research notes", but the role-specific tool for filing research notes is gone and no replacement for research notes appears in the new tools list. Given a research run, the agent cannot add its research notes as its charter promises; it can only file bugs.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-researcher.md:4

chunk_findings.detail: The new line tells the agent to file "any ddflow defect or missing feature you met" at end of run, but [r-ddflow-self-assessment] requires an assessment for bugs of ddflow itself, misbehavior, or missing features at the end of every agent run, phase, and before context compaction, with a duplicate/already-corrected check. A run that happens not to meet an obvious defect is never prompted to assess, and phase/pre-compaction are omitted. The prior probe only checks that this line exists, so it does not answer this.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-researcher.md:15 and ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-reviewer.md:15

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to verify that a hand edit is saved by `adopt --agents claude`, but it never checks the saved-edit sidecar or asserts that the edited content (`"Call it whenever"`) exists anywhere after the second adopt. It only asserts the command succeeded, stdout contains `"your edits are kept in"`, the managed file once again contains `"Call `ddflow_brief` first"`, and `LA.states(repo) == {}`. A broken implementation that refreshes the managed file, prints the notice, and silently discards the user's hand edit would satisfy every assertion; the exact data-loss behavior this test is named for remains unverified.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lean_agents.py:test_adopt_refreshes_a_hand_edited_definition_and_saves_the_edit

chunk_findings.detail: The new self-assessment instruction still does not tell the agent to check whether a candidate issue is already corrected. [r-ddflow-self-assessment] explicitly requires checking that discovered items are “not duplicated and not already corrected,” but the template says only “without duplicating a known one.” Given an agent running on an older ddflow checkout that meets a bug already fixed in the current ddflow code and absent from its known-bug list, the agent is instructed to file it, violating the rule.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-implementer.md:15 (same line in ddflow-researcher.md:15 and ddflow-reviewer.md:15)

chunk_findings.detail: The `description` value is an unquoted YAML plain scalar containing the sequence `: ` (`... end to end: claim ...`). In YAML, `: ` is a mapping-value indicator and is not allowed inside a plain scalar; standard YAML parsers (PyYAML/js-yaml) will fail with an error such as `mapping values are not allowed here`. This makes the entire frontmatter invalid, so the `ddflow-implementer` agent definition cannot be loaded by `ddflow adopt`/Claude Code.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-implementer.md:3

chunk_findings.detail: The body instructs "Call `ddflow_brief` first" and later refers to `ddflow_research_add`, `ddflow_recall`, `ddflow_help`, and `ddflow_rule_show` without the MCP prefix, but the frontmatter only grants `mcp__ddflow__ddflow_brief`, `mcp__ddflow__ddflow_research_add`, etc. A generated subagent that follows the instruction literally will attempt a tool named `ddflow_brief`, which does not exist in its tool list and is rejected by Claude Code, so the role cannot perform its required first action.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-researcher.md:11 and ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-reviewer.md:11

chunk_findings.detail: These generated role definitions omit the mandatory ddflow self-assessment step required at the end of every agent run, phase, and before context compaction, and the instruction to file discovered ddflow bugs/misbehavior/missing features without duplicates. As written, nothing in either contract tells the researcher or reviewer to self-assess ddflow itself, violating [r-ddflow-self-assessment].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-researcher.md:8-15 and ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-reviewer.md:8-15

chunk_findings.detail:
`_front` turns a YAML block list into a Python list, so `tools = [t.strip() for t in str(fm["tools"]).split(",")]` is not a valid parser for the generated templates when `tools:` is written as:

```
tools:
  - Bash
  - Read
  - mcp__ddflow__ddflow_brief
```

In that case `fm["tools"]` is `['Bash', 'Read', 'mcp__ddflow__ddflow_brief']`, and `str(...).split(",")` produces tokens like `"['Bash'"` and `"'mcp__ddflow__ddflow_brief']"`, none of which equals `"mcp__ddflow__ddflow_brief"`. The assertion then fails for every role, even though the definition correctly names `ddflow_brief`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lean_agents.py:48

chunk_findings.detail: [r-ddflow-self-assessment] The added self-assessment instruction only triggers “At the end of the run,” but the recorded rule requires assessment “at the end of every agent run, phase and before context compaction.” A concrete failure remains: an implementer agent whose context is compacted mid-run after encountering a ddflow bug has no instruction to file it at that point, so the defect can be lost before the run ends.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-implementer.md:15

chunk_findings.detail: The added line only covers the “end of the run” trigger from [r-ddflow-self-assessment]. The rule also requires the ddflow self-assessment at the end of each phase and before compacting the subagent context window; neither template tells the agent to file defects at those boundaries. Example: a researcher subagent whose context is compacted mid-run and then continues is never instructed to file defects found before compaction, so the prior “confirmed” fix does not fully answer the finding.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-researcher.md:15 (also ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-reviewer.md:15)

chunk_findings.detail: The test never asserts that the hand edit (`"Call it whenever"`) is actually saved anywhere after the second `adopt`; it only checks that the canonical `"Call `ddflow_brief` first"` is restored and that stdout contains `"your edits are kept in"`. A broken implementation that discards the edit and unconditionally prints that message would still pass this test, so the regression the test name claims to guard against is not actually verified.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lean_agents.py:test_adopt_refreshes_a_hand_edited_definition_and_saves_the_edit

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten self-assessment sentence still does not fully satisfy [r-ddflow-self-assessment]. It tells the agent to file defects “without duplicating a known one,” but the rule also requires checking that the discovered item is “not already corrected.” Concrete failure: an agent encounters a defect, the defect is fixed before the end of the phase, and at the phase boundary the instruction gives it no requirement to re-check current state, so it can file a stale `ddflow_bug_found` report the rule was meant to prevent.

chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-researcher.md:3 and ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-reviewer.md:3

chunk_findings.detail: Both roles state "Never edits files" / "You edit no file", but the `tools:` list includes `Bash`. Claude Code's Bash has no read-only mode, so the agent can execute mutating shell commands such as `sed -i 's/TODO/FIXME/g' src/*.py` or `echo > file`; the read-only guarantee is prose only and is not enforced by the agent definition an input that asks for a repo-wide edit can modify files.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-researcher.md:4 and ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-reviewer.md:4

chunk_findings.detail: The test invokes `run_cli(repo, "adopt", "--agents", "cursor")` but discards the exit code and any stderr, then only checks that `.claude/agents` does not exist. Given a broken implementation where `adopt --agents cursor` immediately exits non-zero before writing any files, the assertion still passes, so the test is vacuously true under exactly the failure mode it should distinguish from a successful non-Claude adoption. It should first assert the command succeeded and that the intended cursor files were written before asserting no Claude definitions are produced.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lean_agents.py:test_adopt_for_another_agent_writes_no_claude_definitions

chunk_findings.detail: The added line only instructs the implementer to file ddflow defects “At the end of the run.” [r-ddflow-self-assessment] also requires the assessment at the end of every phase and before context compaction. Given an implementer run that compacts context before the run ends, an ddflow bug visible only in the discarded context is never filed because the only instruction occurs later, so the new line does not fully answer the role’s self-assessment obligation.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-implementer.md:15

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten `drift_notes()` message is still unconditional for every non-current state: it says `ddflow adopt --agents claude` “rewrites the managed region (a hand edit is saved beside the file).” For a missing definition, e.g. a repo where `.claude/agents/ddflow-researcher.md` does not exist and `states()` reports that path as `missing`, there is no managed region and no hand edit to save; adopt creates a fresh template instead, so the note gives false recovery information for that state.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leanagents.py:100

chunk_findings.detail: The tools line drops `mcp__ddflow__ddflow_research_add` and inserts `mcp__ddflow__ddflow_bug_found`. The description still says the researcher "files research notes", but the role-specific tool for filing research notes is gone and no replacement for research notes appears in the new tools list. Given a research run, the agent cannot add its research notes as its charter promises; it can only file bugs.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-researcher.md:4

chunk_findings.detail: The new line tells the agent to file "any ddflow defect or missing feature you met" at end of run, but [r-ddflow-self-assessment] requires an assessment for bugs of ddflow itself, misbehavior, or missing features at the end of every agent run, phase, and before context compaction, with a duplicate/already-corrected check. A run that happens not to meet an obvious defect is never prompted to assess, and phase/pre-compaction are omitted. The prior probe only checks that this line exists, so it does not answer this.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-researcher.md:15 and ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-reviewer.md:15

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to verify that a hand edit is saved by `adopt --agents claude`, but it never checks the saved-edit sidecar or asserts that the edited content (`"Call it whenever"`) exists anywhere after the second adopt. It only asserts the command succeeded, stdout contains `"your edits are kept in"`, the managed file once again contains `"Call `ddflow_brief` first"`, and `LA.states(repo) == {}`. A broken implementation that refreshes the managed file, prints the notice, and silently discards the user's hand edit would satisfy every assertion; the exact data-loss behavior this test is named for remains unverified.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lean_agents.py:test_adopt_refreshes_a_hand_edited_definition_and_saves_the_edit

chunk_findings.detail: The new self-assessment instruction still does not tell the agent to check whether a candidate issue is already corrected. [r-ddflow-self-assessment] explicitly requires checking that discovered items are “not duplicated and not already corrected,” but the template says only “without duplicating a known one.” Given an agent running on an older ddflow checkout that meets a bug already fixed in the current ddflow code and absent from its known-bug list, the agent is instructed to file it, violating the rule.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-implementer.md:15 (same line in ddflow-researcher.md:15 and ddflow-reviewer.md:15)

chunk_findings.detail: The changed assertion now requires only `"ddflow_bug_found"` and `"already corrected"` in each role body, dropping the previous check for `"before your context is compacted"`. This weakens the test against [r-ddflow-self-assessment]: an implementation that deletes the “before your context is compacted” self-assessment trigger from the templates while leaving `ddflow_bug_found` and `"already corrected"` present would still pass, silently allowing a regression of a required assessment trigger.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lean_agents.py:154

chunk_findings.detail: The `description` value is an unquoted YAML plain scalar containing the sequence `: ` (`... end to end: claim ...`). In YAML, `: ` is a mapping-value indicator and is not allowed inside a plain scalar; standard YAML parsers (PyYAML/js-yaml) will fail with an error such as `mapping values are not allowed here`. This makes the entire frontmatter invalid, so the `ddflow-implementer` agent definition cannot be loaded by `ddflow adopt`/Claude Code.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-implementer.md:3

chunk_findings.detail: The body instructs "Call `ddflow_brief` first" and later refers to `ddflow_research_add`, `ddflow_recall`, `ddflow_help`, and `ddflow_rule_show` without the MCP prefix, but the frontmatter only grants `mcp__ddflow__ddflow_brief`, `mcp__ddflow__ddflow_research_add`, etc. A generated subagent that follows the instruction literally will attempt a tool named `ddflow_brief`, which does not exist in its tool list and is rejected by Claude Code, so the role cannot perform its required first action.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-researcher.md:11 and ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-reviewer.md:11

chunk_findings.detail: These generated role definitions omit the mandatory ddflow self-assessment step required at the end of every agent run, phase, and before context compaction, and the instruction to file discovered ddflow bugs/misbehavior/missing features without duplicates. As written, nothing in either contract tells the researcher or reviewer to self-assess ddflow itself, violating [r-ddflow-self-assessment].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-researcher.md:8-15 and ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-reviewer.md:8-15

chunk_findings.detail:
`_front` turns a YAML block list into a Python list, so `tools = [t.strip() for t in str(fm["tools"]).split(",")]` is not a valid parser for the generated templates when `tools:` is written as:

```
tools:
  - Bash
  - Read
  - mcp__ddflow__ddflow_brief
```

In that case `fm["tools"]` is `['Bash', 'Read', 'mcp__ddflow__ddflow_brief']`, and `str(...).split(",")` produces tokens like `"['Bash'"` and `"'mcp__ddflow__ddflow_brief']"`, none of which equals `"mcp__ddflow__ddflow_brief"`. The assertion then fails for every role, even though the definition correctly names `ddflow_brief`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lean_agents.py:48

chunk_findings.detail: [r-ddflow-self-assessment] The added self-assessment instruction only triggers “At the end of the run,” but the recorded rule requires assessment “at the end of every agent run, phase and before context compaction.” A concrete failure remains: an implementer agent whose context is compacted mid-run after encountering a ddflow bug has no instruction to file it at that point, so the defect can be lost before the run ends.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-implementer.md:15

chunk_findings.detail: The added line only covers the “end of the run” trigger from [r-ddflow-self-assessment]. The rule also requires the ddflow self-assessment at the end of each phase and before compacting the subagent context window; neither template tells the agent to file defects at those boundaries. Example: a researcher subagent whose context is compacted mid-run and then continues is never instructed to file defects found before compaction, so the prior “confirmed” fix does not fully answer the finding.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-researcher.md:15 (also ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-reviewer.md:15)

chunk_findings.detail: The test never asserts that the hand edit (`"Call it whenever"`) is actually saved anywhere after the second `adopt`; it only checks that the canonical `"Call `ddflow_brief` first"` is restored and that stdout contains `"your edits are kept in"`. A broken implementation that discards the edit and unconditionally prints that message would still pass this test, so the regression the test name claims to guard against is not actually verified.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lean_agents.py:test_adopt_refreshes_a_hand_edited_definition_and_saves_the_edit

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten self-assessment sentence still does not fully satisfy [r-ddflow-self-assessment]. It tells the agent to file defects “without duplicating a known one,” but the rule also requires checking that the discovered item is “not already corrected.” Concrete failure: an agent encounters a defect, the defect is fixed before the end of the phase, and at the phase boundary the instruction gives it no requirement to re-check current state, so it can file a stale `ddflow_bug_found` report the rule was meant to prevent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-implementer.md:15 (also ddflow-researcher.md:15 and ddflow-reviewer.md:15)

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion in `test_every_role_is_told_to_file_ddflow_defects_it_meets` was changed from checking for `"before your context is compacted"` to checking for `"already corrected"`. That removes the visible test coverage for the context-compaction trigger required by [r-ddflow-self-assessment]. A template body containing `ddflow_bug_found` and `already corrected` but omitting `before your context is compacted` would still pass this test, so the regression it previously guarded against is no longer caught by the test that now claims to verify the self-assessment requirement.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lean_agents.py:154

chunk_findings.detail: The previous confirmed issue still holds, and this diff does not fix it. The diff only changes `test_every_role_is_told_to_file_ddflow_defects_it_meets`; it leaves `test_adopt_refreshes_a_hand_edited_definition_and_saves_the_edit` asserting only that the canonical `"Call `ddflow_brief` first"` is restored and that stdout contains `"your edits are kept in"`. It never asserts the hand edit `"Call it whenever"` is actually saved, so an implementation that discards the edit and unconditionally prints the message still passes. The triage note (“probe: test reads the .local-edits file”) does not answer the finding because no such read/assertion is present in the change.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lean_agents.py:test_adopt_refreshes_a_hand_edited_definition_and_saves_the_edit

chunk_findings.detail: `deferral_note` early-returns only for `tier == "core"`, but its own docstring says it is empty on both the `core` and `standard` tiers. Concrete input: `deferral_note({"ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH": "false"}, tier="standard")` returns the warning string instead of `""`. Since `standard` is one of the documented known `[mcp].worker_tools` tiers, doctor will emit a "start workers on the `core` tier" warning for a tier the function explicitly promises to treat as already smaller.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:deferral_note

chunk_findings.detail: `recipe()` hardcodes "starts ddflow on the `core` tier" even though `config_text()` and `write()` accept and persist other tiers such as `standard` or `all`. For example, after `write(repo, entry, "standard")`, the returned/printed recipe still claims the resulting `worker-mcp.json` starts the `core` tier, but `config_text` writes `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS: "standard"`. The function has no tier parameter, so it cannot describe a non-core worker config correctly.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:recipe

chunk_findings.detail: `test_doctor_carries_the_note` never clears or pins `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS` before running `doctor`. If the test runner environment has `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=core` (a value this change itself makes the default for lane workers), the first doctor run operates on the core tier. Per `test_the_doctor_note_says_when_a_host_would_send_every_schema` on line 94, `deferral_note({"ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH": "false"}, tier="core")` returns `""`, so the note `"every ddflow schema"` is absent and the assertion on line 104 fails. The test should set `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS` to `"all"` or delete it via `monkeypatch.delenv("DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS", raising=False)` for this doctor phase.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_worker_mcp_config.py:104

chunk_findings.detail: The per-lane override in the launch template is ignored when generating the worker MCP config. `tier` is read only from `Config.load(repo).mcp.worker_tools` and passed to `WM.write`; the `launch` string that carries the lane-level `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS` override is not consulted. For example, with repo config `[mcp] worker_tools = "all"` and a launch template entry `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=core`, this function passes `"all"` to `WM.write`, so the written worker config does not match the lane's actual worker tier.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt.py:_claude_extras

chunk_findings.detail: The function’s docstring states it is empty on the `core`/`standard` tiers, but the implementation returns early only for `tier == "core"`. Given `tier="standard"` and `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false` (or an `auto:N` at/above 50), the function reaches the final return and emits a “start workers on the `core` tier” doctor note. That contradicts the documented contract and produces a false warning for a `standard` tier user (or the docstring is wrong about `standard`); either the early return must include `standard` or the docstring must not claim it does.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:deferral_note

chunk_findings.detail: The test expects the doctor note when `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false`, but it only monkeypatches that variable and leaves `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS` inherited from the test-runner environment. Run the suite with `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=core` set (a value the feature itself promotes), and the `ddflow doctor` subprocess inherits `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=core`; the doctor then sees tier `core`, where `deferral_note(..., tier="core") == ""` as asserted earlier in the same file, so the note is absent and `json.loads(out)["notes"]` has no “every ddflow schema” entry, failing the assertion despite correct behavior. The pin step should refuse to re-record a transcript whose upgrade cases newly fail, or the manifest should be linted at test time (a unit test loading every unreleased fragment).

chunk_findings.detail: `"run" in args` treats any Docker argument equal to `"run"` as if it were the Docker `run` subcommand. For an entry `{"command": "docker", "args": ["exec", "worker", "run"]}`, `args.index("run")` returns 2, so the code produces `docker exec worker run -e DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=core`. The `-e` ends up after the `CONTAINER COMMAND` position, so Docker passes it as an argument to the container command `run` instead of setting the environment, and the env var is not forwarded to the container.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:34

chunk_findings.detail: Even for a real `docker run`, the inserted `-e` is placed before existing Docker options. Docker applies repeated `-e KEY=value` options in order and the last one wins. Given `entry = {"command": "docker", "args": ["run", "-e", "DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=all", "image"]}` and `tier="core"`, the output is `docker run -e DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=core -e DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=all image`, so the container receives `all` rather than the configured `core`. The function's `out["env"]` line already overrides an existing env value for non-Docker entries, so the Docker path should likewise win.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:36

chunk_findings.detail: The new Docker `-e` forwarding inserts `-e DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=<tier>` immediately after the first `"run"` token, before any existing `-e`/`--env DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=...` entries in the original `args`. Docker treats a duplicated `-e` environment variable as last-one-wins, so a later existing value overrides the intended tier. Example: for `{"command": "docker", "args": ["run", "-e", "DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=all", "ddflow:latest"]}` and `tier="core"`, the returned args are `["run", "-e", "DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=core", "-e", "DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=all", "ddflow:latest"]`; the container gets `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=all`, not `core`. The function is supposed to force the worker tier, so the lane override is silently lost when the Docker launch already forwards `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS`. It should remove or replace existing `-e DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS`/`--env DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS` entries, or insert the override after them.

Per `test_the_doctor_note_says_when_a_host_would_send_every_schema` on line 94, `deferral_note({"ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH": "false"}, tier="core")` returns `""`, so the note `"every ddflow schema"` is absent and the assertion on line 104 fails. The test should set `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS` to `"all"` or delete it via `monkeypatch.delenv("DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS", raising=False)` for this doctor phase.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_worker_mcp_config.py:104

chunk_findings.detail: `recipe(tier="all")` (reachable from `adopt.py`, which passes `Config.load(repo).mcp.worker_tools`) now starts with "starts ddflow on the `all` tier" but still ends with "which the core tier keeps small." On the `all` tier the full ~84.2K schema list is what gets sent when `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false`, so the advice is false for every non-core tier; the new test only checks that "`standard` tier" appears and "`core` tier" does not appear in the first clause, so this remaining hardcoded claim is missed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:recipe

chunk_findings.detail: The new test does not clear or pin `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS` before invoking `adopt`. If the test runner has `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=core` set — the lane-worker default this change itself introduces, and the same condition that forced the doctor test correction above — `run_cli(repo, "adopt", "--agents", "claude")` resolves `Config.load(repo).mcp.worker_tools` from that environment variable rather than the `config --set mcp.worker_tools standard` file, so the output contains "`core` tier" and `assert "`standard` tier" in out` fails. It needs `monkeypatch.delenv("DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS", raising=False)` or a pinned value like the doctor test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_worker_mcp_config.py:test_the_recipe_names_the_tier_the_file_carries

chunk_findings.detail: `"run" in args` treats any Docker argument equal to `"run"` as if it were the Docker `run` subcommand. For an entry `{"command": "docker", "args": ["exec", "worker", "run"]}`, `args.index("run")` returns 2, so the code produces `docker exec worker run -e DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=core`. The `-e` ends up after the `CONTAINER COMMAND` position, so Docker passes it as an argument to the container command `run` instead of setting the environment, and the env var is not forwarded to the container.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:34

chunk_findings.detail: Even for a real `docker run`, the inserted `-e` is placed before existing Docker options. Docker applies repeated `-e KEY=value` options in order and the last one wins. Given `entry = {"command": "docker", "args": ["run", "-e", "DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=all", "image"]}` and `tier="core"`, the output is `docker run -e DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=core -e DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=all image`, so the container receives `all` rather than the configured `core`. The function's `out["env"]` line already overrides an existing env value for non-Docker entries, so the Docker path should likewise win.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:36

chunk_findings.detail: `args[:1] == ["run"]` only recognizes `docker run` when `run` is the first argument. Docker allows global options before the command, e.g. `{"command": "docker", "args": ["--host", "tcp://...", "run", "img"]}`. For that entry with `tier="core"`, the condition is false, so the `-e DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=core` forwarding is never added; `out["env"]` only sets the env for the docker client, not the container. Valid `docker run` invocations therefore silently miss the configured tier.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:worker_entry

chunk_findings.detail: `_without_tier` removes matching `-e`/`--env` pairs from the entire `args[1:]` slice without stopping at the image/command boundary. Example: `worker_entry({"command": "docker", "args": ["run", "img", "mycmd", "-e", "DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=all"]}, "core")` returns `["run", "-e", "DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=core", "img", "mycmd"]` because `_without_tier` deletes the `-e DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=all` arguments. But after `img`, Docker treats those two arguments as the container command's own arguments, not as docker run options, so the function corrupts the container command rather than replacing a forwarded tier. The removal must stop once the IMAGE argument is reached.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:_without_tier

evidence.diff_source: delta review of 1 commit since f7963ac2f2

chunk_findings.detail: The per-lane override in the launch template is ignored when generating the worker MCP config. `tier` is read only from `Config.load(repo).mcp.worker_tools` and passed to `WM.write`; the `launch` string that carries the lane-level `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS` override is not consulted. For example, with repo config `[mcp] worker_tools = "all"` and a launch template entry `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=core`, this function passes `"all"` to `WM.write`, so the written worker config does not match the lane's actual worker tier.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt.py:_claude_extras

chunk_findings.detail: The function’s docstring states it is empty on the `core`/`standard` tiers, but the implementation returns early only for `tier == "core"`. Given `tier="standard"` and `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false` (or an `auto:N` at/above 50), the function reaches the final return and emits a “start workers on the `core` tier” doctor note. That contradicts the documented contract and produces a false warning for a `standard` tier user (or the docstring is wrong about `standard`); either the early return must include `standard` or the docstring must not claim it does.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:deferral_note

chunk_findings.detail: The test expects the doctor note when `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false`, but it only monkeypatches that variable and leaves `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS` inherited from the test-runner environment. Run the suite with `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=core` set (a value the feature itself promotes), and the `ddflow doctor` subprocess inherits `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=core`; the doctor then sees tier `core`, where `deferral_note(..., tier="core") == ""` as asserted earlier in the same file, so the note is absent and `json.loads(out)["notes"]` has no “every ddflow schema” entry, failing the assertion despite correct behavior. The test should explicitly set or delete `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS` to `"all"` for this scenario.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_worker_mcp_config.py:test_doctor_carries_the_note

chunk_findings.detail: The new Docker `-e` forwarding inserts `-e DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=<tier>` immediately after the first `"run"` token, before any existing `-e`/`--env DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=...` entries in the original `args`. Docker treats a duplicated `-e` environment variable as last-one-wins, so a later existing value overrides the intended tier. Example: for `{"command": "docker", "args": ["run", "-e", "DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=all", "ddflow:latest"]}` and `tier="core"`, the returned args are `["run", "-e", "DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=core", "-e", "DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=all", "ddflow:latest"]`; the container gets `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=all`, not `core`. The function is supposed to force the worker tier, so the lane override is silently lost when the Docker launch already forwards `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS`. It should remove or replace existing `-e DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS`/`--env DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS` entries, or insert the override after them.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:with_tier

chunk_findings.detail: `_without_tier` scans the whole argument list after `run` and deletes any `-e|--env DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS` pair, but Docker stops option parsing at the image name; after the image those tokens are container command arguments. For `entry = {"command": "docker", "args": ["run", "alpine", "echo", "-e", "DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=all"]}` and `tier="core"`, `worker_entry` returns `["run", "-e", "DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=core", "alpine", "echo"]`; the container command `echo -e DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=all` is corrupted to `echo`. The stripping must stop at the image/container-command boundary.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:_without_tier

chunk_findings.detail: The forwarding gate is now `args[:1] == ["run"]`, but valid Docker global flags can precede the subcommand. Given `{"command": "docker", "args": ["--context", "remote", "run", "-it", "img"]}` and `tier="core"`, the condition is false, so no `-e DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=core` is added; `out["env"]` only sets the docker client environment, not the container environment. The previous `"run" in args` logic handled this, so the new narrowing is a regression.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:worker_entry

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 2 still holds: this diff has no hunk for `deferral_note`. It still returns early only for `tier == "core"`; with `tier="standard"` and `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false` (or `auto:N` at/above 50) it reaches the final return and emits the “start workers on the `core` tier” note, contradicting the documented `core`/`standard` contract.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:deferral_note

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 3 still holds: this diff adds only worker_entry tests and does not modify `test_doctor_carries_the_note`. That test monkeypatches only `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false` and inherits `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS`; run the suite with `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS=core`, and the `ddflow doctor` subprocess inherits `core`, so `deferral_note` returns `""` and the asserted note is absent, making the test fail.

chunk_findings.detail: `0` is accepted and documented as “no ceiling at that level”, but the same knob doc also says the effective budget is “the smaller of the global and its type's”. With `[session] context_budget_tokens = 30000` and `[session.context_budget] claude = 0`, the type-level 0 is a sentinel meaning “no type-specific ceiling”, so Claude should still be constrained by the global 30000. A literal `min(context_budget_tokens, context_budget["claude"])` returns 0, which either treats the sentinel as an actual zero-token budget or silently disables the global ceiling. The sentinel must be ignored/lifted when computing the effective budget, not fed to `min`.

chunk_findings.detail: The new table has a `global` key, but `context_budget_problem` validates only the table in isolation; nothing enforces the stated alias that `[session].context_budget_tokens` and `[session.context_budget].global` have the same value. Input: `context_budget_tokens = 10000` and `[session.context_budget] global = 50000` passes validation, leaving two different global budgets. chunk_findings.detail: `report` ignores its `agent` argument when selecting the headline budget and instead detects a harness from the current process environment via `HR.detect(os.environ)`. `agent` is the session's agent type from the harness/clientInfo: it is the value used for `start_texts(repo, agent)` and the intent says the target is “agent type from the harness/clientInfo of the session.” If a stored session has agent type `claude` with `[session.context_budget].claude = 20000` (global 100000), but the doctor is run in a process whose environment is detected as a different harness (or none), `effective_budget(cfg.session, HR.detect(os.environ))` returns 100000. chunk_findings.detail: The test sets `_session(context_budget_tokens=40000, context_budget={"global": 30000})` and asserts `SC.effective_budget(s, "claude") == 30000`. chunk_findings.detail: The new knob documents `0` as “no ceiling at that level” while also defining the effective budget as the smaller of the global and per-type values. Since all values are non-negative and `0` is the sentinel for “no ceiling,” `min(global, type)` is zero whenever either layer is `0`. For example, with `context_budget_tokens = 30000` and `[session.context_budget] claude = 0`, the intended meaning of the per-type `0` is to remove only the claude-specific limit, leaving the global 30000 in effect. But the min formula produces effective budget `0`; because `0` is then interpreted as “no budget,” the global budget is silently disabled for claude. If `0` were instead interpreted as a literal zero-token budget, then the documented global `0` (“no budget”) would zero out every session. Either way the knobs are not independently configurable as the change requires.

chunk_findings.detail: `report` chooses the target for the headline budget from `HR.detect(os.environ)` and ignores the `agent` argument it already receives. chunk_findings.detail: The final block claims to verify “the later layer's spelling wins, whichever knob it uses”, but it only asserts `Config.load(repo).session.context_budget_tokens == 12000`. The test would still pass while the local scalar override incorrectly wipes out agent-type budgets. The intended “Regression/ratchet test per target” is not actually enforced for the layered-override case.

chunk_findings.detail: The change still does not fix prior finding #4; it codifies it. The new test `test_the_table_global_key_is_a_second_spelling_of_the_global_and_the_smaller_wins` asserts that `_session(context_budget_tokens=40000, context_budget={"global": 30000})` gives `SC.effective_budget(s, "claude") == 30000`. That treats `[session.context_budget].global` as an independent second ceiling instead of an alias. The stated intent for this change is that `[session].context_budget_tokens` alias `[session.context_budget].global` and they are the *same value*; conflicting values should be invalid, not silently reduced to the smaller. The new doc line says “if both are set the smaller applies,” directly contradicting that intent, so the invalid config `context_budget_tokens = 40000` plus `[session.context_budget] global = 30000` still silently changes the budget to 30000.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_context_budget_per_agent.py:46 (and ddflow/config_sections/session.py:120)

chunk_findings.detail: `effective_budget` no longer reads `session.context_budget["global"]`; the global table key is folded into `context_budget_tokens` only as a side effect in `ddflow/config.py` while loading config layers. A `Session` object constructed directly with the field shape the knob documents as valid — e.g. `_session(context_budget_tokens=0, context_budget={"global": 30000})` — produces `levels = [0, 0]` for target `"claude"`, and the function returns 0. That silently drops the 30000-token global budget. The `context_budget` knob doc still says `global` “is another spelling of `context_budget_tokens`,” so any path that bypasses the config-layer loader sees wrong output; the service should resolve `global` from the dict itself rather than depend on the loader pop.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/startcost.py:effective_budget

chunk_findings.detail: The final block claims to verify “the later layer's spelling wins, whichever knob it uses”, but it only asserts `Config.load(repo).session.context_budget_tokens == 12000`. It never asserts the resulting per-agent effective budgets after the local scalar override. The repository layer set `claude = 25000`; since 25000 is higher than the later global 12000, both the correct merge (claude remains 25000, so `min(12000, 25000) == 12000`) and a buggy “later scalar section replaces the whole context_budget dict” (claude is dropped, fallback global also 12000) produce the same effective budget for claude. The test would still pass while the local scalar override incorrectly wipes out agent-type budgets. The intended “Regression/ratchet test per target” is not actually enforced for the layered-override case.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_context_budget_per_agent.py:57

evidence.note: ruff clean; roborev_branch clean on the 3rd pass (global validation, provenance, unknown type, complexity fixed)

chunk_findings.detail: The new knob documents `0` as “no ceiling at that level” while also defining the effective budget as the smaller of the global and per-type values. Since all values are non-negative and `0` is the sentinel for “no ceiling,” `min(global, type)` is zero whenever either layer is `0`. For example, with `context_budget_tokens = 30000` and `[session.context_budget] claude = 0`, the intended meaning of the per-type `0` is to remove only the claude-specific limit, leaving the global 30000 in effect. But the min formula produces effective budget `0`; because `0` is then interpreted as “no budget,” the global budget is silently disabled for claude. If `0` were instead interpreted as a literal zero-token budget, then the documented global `0` (“no budget”) would zero out every session. Either way the knobs are not independently configurable as the change requires.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/session.py: context_budget

chunk_findings.detail: `report` chooses the target for the headline budget from `HR.detect(os.environ)` and ignores the `agent` argument it already receives. If a report is generated for the session whose agent/clientInfo is `agent="claude"` while the ddflow process environment has no recognized harness (`HR.detect` returns `""`), then with `session.context_budget_tokens=1000` and `session.context_budget={"claude": 500}`, `effective_budget(cfg.session, HR.detect(os.environ))` returns `1000` instead of `500`. The reported `StartCost.budget` is therefore wrong for that session, and the doctor line can incorrectly say no OVER against the session's actual 500-token claude cap. The session target should be taken from `agent` (the value also passed to `start_texts(repo, agent)`), not from the ambient process environment.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/startcost.py report

chunk_findings.detail: `new = '{}'` is a TOML string literal `"{}"`, not an empty TOML table. The change declares a table knob `session.context_budget` whose keys are intended to be `global` and agent-type names, but the upgrade record would set the default to a string. On a system applying this unreleased change with no existing `session.context_budget` key, lookups such as `session.context_budget.global` or `session.context_budget.claude` fail because the value is a string, not a mapping. Use `new = {}` for an empty table.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.session.context_budget.toml:6

chunk_findings.detail: The test sets the two documented aliases to different values (`context_budget_tokens=0` and `context_budget["global"]=30000`) and then asserts `SC.effective_budget(s, "x") == 30000`. This contradicts the change intent that `[session].context_budget_tokens` and `[session.context_budget].global` are the same value and that effective budget is `min(context_budget_tokens, context_budget.<agent type>)`; for an unset target `"x"` the min of `0` and inherited `30000` is `0`. The test therefore enforces the undocumented precedence that the table global key overrides the global knob, or it will fail against a correct min implementation.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_context_budget_per_agent.py:test_the_table_has_its_own_global_key_that_is_the_same_ceiling

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 4 still holds. The renamed test still exercises the disputed case: `_session(context_budget_tokens=0, context_budget={"global": 30000, "claude": 25000})`, then asserts `SC.effective_budget(s, "claude") == 25000` and `SC.effective_budget(s, "x") == 30000`. The knob doc this commit adds says `global` is a second spelling of `context_budget_tokens` and “if both are set the smaller applies”; under that rule the two global spellings `0` and `30000` would resolve to `0`, so the effective claude budget would be `min(0, 25000) == 0` and unset `x` would be `0`, not the asserted `25000`/`30000`. Renaming the test and adding that phrase does not answer the original defect: the exact contradictory assertion remains.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_context_budget_per_agent.py:48-49

chunk_findings.detail: The new fold still resolves the two documented global spellings by assignment, not by the “if both are set the smaller applies” rule. Given TOML written with `[session] context_budget_tokens = 500` followed by `[session.context_budget] global = 800`, the table key is applied after the scalar key, so `_fold_budget_global` executes `target.context_budget_tokens = value.pop("global")` and overwrites `500` with `800`. The final session has `context_budget_tokens=800` and no table `global`, so `effective_budget` returns `800`, whereas the documented smaller-applies behavior is `500`. The outcome is therefore dependent on the order the two alias keys are applied.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config.py:_fold_budget_global

chunk_findings.detail: The added assertion expects `SC.effective_budget(_session(context_budget_tokens=0, context_budget={"global": 30000}), "x") == 30000`. This contradicts the stated rule that `[session].context_budget_tokens` and `[session.context_budget].global` are the same global ceiling and the effective budget is `min(context_budget_tokens, context_budget.<agent type>)`. With the two global spellings set to `0` and `30000`, the smaller applies, so an unset type `"x"` inherits `30000`, and `min(0, 30000)` is `0`, not `30000`. This ratchet test therefore locks in the same wrong behavior from the prior confirmed finding and will force the implementation to violate the intended per-agent budget layering.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_context_budget_per_agent.py:64-68

evidence.budget_forced: fifth round (lead: fifth authorized under the operator's 4-5 range)

chunk_findings.detail:
The new fold operation does not enforce the documented “smaller applies” alias semantics when both spellings of the global budget are present in the same config layer. `_fold_budget_global` copies `[session.context_budget].global` into `context_budget_tokens` only while the table key is being assigned; a later assignment of `session.context_budget_tokens` in the same layer overwrites it (or the reverse, depending on layer key iteration order). Concrete input:

```toml
[session]
context_budget_tokens = 50000
[session.context_budget]
global = 10000
```

If the table key is processed before the scalar key, `target.context_budget_tokens` is first folded to `10000` and then overwritten to `50000`; the effective global becomes `50000`, above the `10000` declared as the smaller global. The loader still lets one spelling silently win instead of applying the smaller value.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config.py:_fold_budget_global

chunk_findings.detail: The previous confirmed alias-conflict issue still holds. `context_budget_problem` is attached only to the `context_budget` table and therefore never sees the scalar `context_budget_tokens`. Input `[session] context_budget_tokens = 10000` plus `[session.context_budget] global = 50000` passes this check, but the knob doc in this same diff says `global` is “another spelling of `context_budget_tokens`: the same value.” The “later layer’s spelling winning” rule does not resolve a same-layer conflict, so the operator gets two different global ceilings and no validation error; if `config.py` later folds one into the other, that fold is not declared by this section’s check or doc.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/session.py:context_budget_problem

chunk_findings.detail: `report` is where the doctor line is produced, but this diff never passes the new per-target budgets into `measure`. `measure` now accepts `targets` and defaults it to `{}`, and `StartCost.__str__` prints target lines only from `self.targets`; however `report` is not modified to call `effective_budget`/`configured_targets`, so `report(...).targets` is always empty. Concrete failure: with `[session] context_budget_tokens = 100000` and `[session.context_budget] claude = 20000`, `report(repo, cfg, "claude", start_texts).notes()` emits the global line but no `claude: N tokens (budget 20000)` line, so the per-agent doctor reporting required by the change is silently absent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/startcost.py:report

chunk_findings.detail: The new test codifies that `context_budget_tokens=0` with `context_budget={"claude": 0}` yields an effective budget of `0`, and that `context_budget_tokens=0` with `{"claude": 15000}` yields `codex == 0`. This contradicts this same file's line 7 and the knob doc: `0` means “no ceiling at that level,” and an unset type inherits the global. In the second scenario `codex` inherits the global `0`, so the global setting says “no global ceiling,” yet the effective budget becomes a zero-token budget for every unset type. The operator input `context_budget_tokens=0` plus only `claude=15000` gives claude a 15000 budget while all other agent types are reported as `(budget 0)` and flagged OVER for any non-empty startup text, even though the documented meaning of the global `0` is no ceiling rather than a zero-token limit. The test asserting `codex == 0` green-lights that contradiction.

chunk_findings.detail: `LBS.sizing` is fed `HR.detect(os.environ)`, which identifies the harness running `ddflow brief`, not the agent type named by the command's `--for-agent NAME`. If a coordinator running under Claude renders a brief for `codex` with `[session.context_budget] global=40000, claude=10000, codex=100000`, this code reads Claude's effective budget 10000 and produces a 4000-character LEAN brief; Codex's effective budget is min(40000, 100000)=40000 and would produce the full 9000-character capped brief. The wrong agent's budget drives the cap and LEAN selection, contradicting the per-agent effective budget rule in [D-session-start-budget].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/briefing.py:103

chunk_findings.detail: `LEAN_OFF` drops the `"lessons"` section, but `LEAN_NOTE`—the line meant to tell the user what a lean brief left out—lists only testing/review/gate/filing and the project's own text. In any lean brief, the lessons are therefore omitted silently, which contradicts the code's own comment that "the omission is said, never silent."
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/launchbrief.py:22 (LEAN_NOTE)

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts `LB.sizing(_session(context_budget_tokens=0, agent_brief_max_chars=0), "").cap == 0`. With the new `session.agent_brief_min_chars` defaulting to 4000 and the stated contract that the cap is never below a floor, this input should produce at least the floor, not a zero-character cap. A `cap == 0` result means the renderer will truncate the launch brief to an empty string (or require an undocumented special case), so this test locks in behavior that undermines the floor knob for a session that has both size sources disabled.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_launch_brief_budget.py:51

chunk_findings.detail: `share` is computed as `int(budget * session.agent_brief_budget_share * session.start_bytes_per_token)`, which produces a **byte** count. But this value is compared against `session.agent_brief_min_chars`/`agent_brief_lean_chars`/`agent_brief_max_chars` and returned as `Sizing.cap`, which line 26 documents as **characters**. For non-ASCII launch-brief text these differ materially: a brief in Chinese or with non-Latin paths can have one CJK character per token while UTF-8 uses 2–4 bytes, so a 2,000-token allowance becomes 4,000–8,000 bytes but only 2,000 characters. A renderer enforcing `cap` as a character count will allow far more CJK text than the start-budget-derived byte budget intends. Use a chars-per-token estimate for a character cap, or make `Sizing.cap`/min/lean byte-denominated.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/launchbrief.py:38

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test's regex for extracting tools from `_base(repo)` is `re.findall(r"`(ddflow_[a-z_]+)", _base(repo))`: it only matches a backtick span that is exactly a tool name with no arguments. But the changed `ddflow/templates/prompts/mcp_instructions.md` line renders the promised tool as `` `ddflow_rule_show id=<id>` `` with ` id=<id>` inside the same backtick pair. The regex cannot match that span because the literal space before `id=<id>` is not allowed by `[a-z_]+` and the closing backtick is not immediately after `rule_show`. Therefore `named` will not contain `ddflow_rule_show`, and the very next line, `assert {"ddflow_brief", "ddflow_rule_show", "ddflow_rule_search"} <= named`, will fail on the fixed code. The new test is broken and breaks CI.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_core_tier_charter_tools.py:28

chunk_findings.detail: The patch sidesteps the new `test_every_tool_the_base_charter_names_is_in_the_core_tier` by deleting the backticked `ddflow_configure` mention from the base charter instead of putting `ddflow_configure` in the core tier. `_LEGACY_STANDARD` still has `"configure"`, so on a core-tier connection that command remains outside `tier_tools("core")`. A core-tier client that follows the updated line to "the manual says how" can still be told to call `ddflow_configure` through the manual, yet the tool is not listed, so the same hidden-tool failure the bug describes persists one hop deeper and the regression test does not cover the manual content.
