chunk_findings.detail: The change removes `desired = head + region.render(body)`, but the unchanged tail of `_write_command` still refers to `desired` when `path` does not exist (the normal “adopt a new file” case). For a repo where `repo/<rel>` is absent, after the `if path.exists():` block the function executes `replace_text(path, desired)` and raises `NameError: name 'desired' is not defined` instead of writing the generated file.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt.py:_write_command

chunk_findings.detail: `block = region.render(body, extra=_head_stamp(use_head))` stamps the kept front matter (`use_head`) rather than the template front matter (`head`). When `head_state == "edited"`, `use_head` is the operator’s hand-edited front matter, so the stamp records the operator’s edit as if ddflow wrote it. On the next adopt run where the template head changes again, `_refresh_head` sees `stamp.extra["head"] == content_digest(have)` and classifies the operator edit as ddflow’s own old front matter (`refresh`), so `_update_managed` silently replaces the hand-edited front matter even though it was supposed to be kept.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt.py:_update_managed

chunk_findings.detail: The new `recipe()` hardcodes the “25.9K first turn with no role” measurement in the sentence that interpolates `{tier}`. For any non-core tier (the function accepts `tier`, and the old text explicitly referred to “other tiers”), e.g. `recipe(rel=".mcp.json", tier="full")`, the returned text says a full-tier config starts with 25.9K with no role, and then gives role measurements that are “on the core tier” while tying the command to the same non-core `{rel}`. The old text deliberately did not attach no-role numbers to the generic `{tier}` command and warned that other tiers were not measured with a role; the new text is false for every tier except `"core"`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:87-93

chunk_findings.detail: The paragraph now says both that `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS` comes from `[mcp].worker_tools` (`core` by default) and that the family names are listed by “the default `lean` profile.” A user cannot tell which profile `ddflow adopt` actually emits; under the bug being fixed the default MCP profile is lean, so the retained “`core` by default” at line 35 is now contradictory/stale and makes the command examples and measured numbers ambiguous about which config they assume.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/mcp.md:35-42

chunk_findings.detail: The table now lists V12 as 26.0K and V10 as 24.2K, so the deferred cost is 1.8K, not 1.4K. The text was not updated with the re-measured values, leaving a directly contradictory number in the revised results.

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test claims to cover “every profile” but only parameterizes `["lean", "families", "hot+families"]`, omitting the `core` profile that the fix itself says requires the flat spellings. Under an implementation that keeps only family names in the role definitions, `LA.ddflow_tools(role)` contains no flat `mcp__ddflow__ddflow_gate_*` entries, so `needed` is empty and the assertion passes, allowing the flat/core side of the “name both spellings” requirement to regress without failing this test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lean_agents.py:test_a_role_can_reach_what_its_work_needs_under_every_profile

chunk_findings.detail: The old test enforced that for `tier="all"` the recipe does **not** contain `"the core-tier config below"` or `"measured on the core tier"`. The new version deletes both negative checks and instead requires `"on the core tier"` to be present. Given a bad `WM.recipe(REL, tier="all")` output that says `"Use the core-tier config below:"`, the test would still pass as long as it also contains `"measured 10.7K for the researcher"` and `"on the core tier"`. The invariant the test is named for is no longer actually enforced.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_worker_mcp_config.py:test_the_recipe_does_not_call_the_configured_tier_core_when_it_is_not

chunk_findings.detail: The old path wrote `desired`, the fully assembled file content. The new path writes only `head + region.render(body, extra=_head_stamp(head))`. `region.render` renders just the managed region, so any managed file with content after that region (the tail) is silently truncated on the next adopt/update. Input: an adopted file that has a managed region followed by user-maintained trailing lines; running the update path drops those trailing lines.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt.py:1239

chunk_findings.detail: The tools list adds family spellings but omits `mcp__ddflow__ddflow_view`. The change manifest states the default lean profile includes the `view` family alongside `gate`, `bug`, `session`, `task`, and `memory`, and the intended fix is to add both flat and family spellings. With the default lean profile, `ddflow-implementer` therefore still cannot reach the `view` family through MCP, so bug B07c4286c92 remains for that family. The added fallback line does not cover this case because the profile does list `view`; it is the role’s `tools:` allow-list that is missing it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-implementer.md:3

chunk_findings.detail: The self-assessment paragraph still tells the researcher to file defects with the flat tool `ddflow_bug_found`. The default/lean MCP profile this patch is fixing does not list that flat name, so under `--profile lean` the researcher has no callable `ddflow_bug_found`; this is precisely the kind of flat-name reference the change is meant to remove. The patch adds the family spelling `mcp__ddflow__ddflow_bug` to `tools:`, but the required end-of-run/phase/compaction filing is still pointed at the unavailable flat tool, so an agent following the explicit instruction can fail to satisfy [r-ddflow-self-assessment] despite having `_bug` available.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-researcher.md:14

chunk_findings.detail: The paragraph still says `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS` comes from `[mcp].worker_tools` with `core` by default, but two lines later it says the family names are the ones “the default `lean` profile lists.” The bug this change fixes is explicitly based on the default MCP profile being `lean`, so these two statements cannot both describe the current default. This will mislead readers about which tool set `ddflow adopt`/worker-mcp actually configures; the `core` parenthetical should be updated to `lean` (or the claim that `lean` is the default removed).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/mcp.md:35 and :42

chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/lean-start-inherit.md: "ddflow's names cost 1.4K deferred (V12 against V10)"

chunk_findings.detail: The new summary says LS-agents’ functional allow-list definitions run “10.7K to 17.8K,” but the table this same change edits lists `ddflow-implementer` (current definition) at **18.2K** (line 70). 18.2K is outside the stated 10.7K–17.8K range, so the document contradicts its own current measured numbers and can mislead anyone using section 4 to choose the implementer definition based on the lower claimed upper bound.

chunk_findings.detail: The old guard asserted `"measured on the core tier" not in text`; the new code replaces that with `"on the core tier" in text`. That inverts the check: if `WM.recipe(REL, tier="all")` returns text such as `starts ddflow on the `all` tier` plus `measured 10.7K for the researcher on the core tier`, the test passes, even though this is the exact kind of core-tier wording the test name says must not appear. chunk_findings.detail: The old path wrote `desired`, the fully assembled file content. The new path writes only `head + region.render(body, extra=_head_stamp(head))`. `region.render` renders just the managed region, so any managed file with content after that region (the tail) is silently truncated on the next adopt/update. Input: an adopted file that has a managed region followed by user-maintained trailing lines; running the update path drops those trailing lines.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt.py:1239

chunk_findings.detail: The tools list adds family spellings but omits `mcp__ddflow__ddflow_view`. The change manifest states the default lean profile includes the `view` family alongside `gate`, `bug`, `session`, `task`, and `memory`, and the intended fix is to add both flat and family spellings. With the default lean profile, `ddflow-implementer` therefore still cannot reach the `view` family through MCP, so bug B07c4286c92 remains for that family. The added fallback line does not cover this case because the profile does list `view`; it is the role’s `tools:` allow-list that is missing it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-implementer.md:3

chunk_findings.detail: The self-assessment paragraph still tells the researcher to file defects with the flat tool `ddflow_bug_found`. The default/lean MCP profile this patch is fixing does not list that flat name, so under `--profile lean` the researcher has no callable `ddflow_bug_found`; this is precisely the kind of flat-name reference the change is meant to remove. The patch adds the family spelling `mcp__ddflow__ddflow_bug` to `tools:`, but the required end-of-run/phase/compaction filing is still pointed at the unavailable flat tool, so an agent following the explicit instruction can fail to satisfy [r-ddflow-self-assessment] despite having `_bug` available.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-researcher.md:14

chunk_findings.detail: The paragraph still says `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS` comes from `[mcp].worker_tools` with `core` by default, but two lines later it says the family names are the ones “the default `lean` profile lists.” The bug this change fixes is explicitly based on the default MCP profile being `lean`, so these two statements cannot both describe the current default. This will mislead readers about which tool set `ddflow adopt`/worker-mcp actually configures; the `core` parenthetical should be updated to `lean` (or the claim that `lean` is the default removed).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/mcp.md:35 and :42

chunk_findings.detail: The diff updates the V12 row from 25.6K to 26.0K while V10 remains 24.2K, but the retained bullet still says ddflow's names cost 1.4K deferred. Using the table’s own re-measured numbers gives 26.0 − 24.2 = 1.8K, so the derived cost is now wrong in the document that is being corrected.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/lean-start-inherit.md: "ddflow's names cost 1.4K deferred (V12 against V10)"

chunk_findings.detail: The new summary says LS-agents’ functional allow-list definitions run “10.7K to 17.8K,” but the table this same change edits lists `ddflow-implementer` (current definition) at **18.2K** (line 70). 18.2K is outside the stated 10.7K–17.8K range, so the document contradicts its own current measured numbers and can mislead anyone using section 4 to choose the implementer definition based on the lower claimed upper bound.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/lean-start-inherit.md:85

chunk_findings.detail: The old guard asserted `"measured on the core tier" not in text`; the new code replaces that with `"on the core tier" in text`. That inverts the check: if `WM.recipe(REL, tier="all")` returns text such as `starts ddflow on the `all` tier` plus `measured 10.7K for the researcher on the core tier`, the test passes, even though this is the exact kind of core-tier wording the test name says must not appear. The regression is no longer caught.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_worker_mcp_config.py:test_the_recipe_does_not_call_the_configured_tier_core_when_it_is_not

chunk_findings.detail: The agreement test now asserts `("10.7K", "17.8K", "25.9K")` in both `WM.recipe(REL)` and the help page, while the new recipe test requires `"11.9K"` in `WM.recipe(REL)`. A help page that drops the `11.9K` measurement but still contains the other three numbers will pass, so the test can miss the disagreement it is meant to detect.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_worker_mcp_config.py:test_the_recipe_and_the_help_page_agree_on_the_commands_and_the_numbers

chunk_findings.detail: The new phrase `measured on the core tier.` is unconditional, so `WM.recipe` now returns a self-contradictory recipe for any non-core `tier`. For example, `WM.recipe(REL, tier="all")` yields text saying the command starts ddflow on the `all` tier while tying the 25.9K no-role number to the `core` tier; this is the exact false core-tier wording `test_the_recipe_does_not_call_the_configured_tier_core_when_it_is_not` was meant to reject. The prior confirmed finding 7 is therefore still present in the product string: the phrasing must be conditional on `tier == "core"` or otherwise avoid pairing a core-tier measurement with a different configured tier.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:90

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test’s hard-coded `need` sets omit `ddflow_session_prompt`, even though the bug being fixed explicitly names `mcp__ddflow__ddflow_session_prompt` among the flat spellings the LS-agent role definitions allow-list and the new test’s own docstring says it guards “the flat spellings the core tier lists.” Because `ddflow_session_prompt` is never in any role’s `need`, `assert names <= have` will not fail if a subsequent change drops that flat tool from the role whose `tools:` currently lists it; the test would still pass while the core-tier flat spelling regresses.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lean_agents.py:test_the_flat_spellings_the_core_tier_lists_stay_allow_listed

chunk_findings.detail: The change removes `desired = head + region.render(body)`, but the unchanged tail of `_write_command` still refers to `desired` when `path` does not exist (the normal “adopt a new file” case). For a repo where `repo/<rel>` is absent, after the `if path.exists():` block the function executes `replace_text(path, desired)` and raises `NameError: name 'desired' is not defined` instead of writing the generated file.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt.py:_write_command

chunk_findings.detail: `block = region.render(body, extra=_head_stamp(use_head))` stamps the kept front matter (`use_head`) rather than the template front matter (`head`). When `head_state == "edited"`, `use_head` is the operator’s hand-edited front matter, so the stamp records the operator’s edit as if ddflow wrote it. On the next adopt run where the template head changes again, `_refresh_head` sees `stamp.extra["head"] == content_digest(have)` and classifies the operator edit as ddflow’s own old front matter (`refresh`), so `_update_managed` silently replaces the hand-edited front matter even though it was supposed to be kept.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/adopt.py:_update_managed

chunk_findings.detail: The new `recipe()` hardcodes the “25.9K first turn with no role” measurement in the sentence that interpolates `{tier}`. For any non-core tier (the function accepts `tier`, and the old text explicitly referred to “other tiers”), e.g. `recipe(rel=".mcp.json", tier="full")`, the returned text says a full-tier config starts with 25.9K with no role, and then gives role measurements that are “on the core tier” while tying the command to the same non-core `{rel}`. The old text deliberately did not attach no-role numbers to the generic `{tier}` command and warned that other tiers were not measured with a role; the new text is false for every tier except `"core"`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/workermcp.py:87-93

chunk_findings.detail: The paragraph now says both that `DDFLOW_MCP_TOOLS` comes from `[mcp].worker_tools` (`core` by default) and that the family names are listed by “the default `lean` profile.” A user cannot tell which profile `ddflow adopt` actually emits; under the bug being fixed the default MCP profile is lean, so the retained “`core` by default” at line 35 is now contradictory/stale and makes the command examples and measured numbers ambiguous about which config they assume.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/mcp.md:35-42

chunk_findings.detail: The table now lists V12 as 26.0K and V10 as 24.2K, so the deferred cost is 1.8K, not 1.4K. The text was not updated with the re-measured values, leaving a directly contradictory number in the revised results.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/lean-start-inherit.md: “ddflow’s names cost 1.4K deferred (V12 against V10)”

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test claims to cover “every profile” but only parameterizes `["lean", "families", "hot+families"]`, omitting the `core` profile that the fix itself says requires the flat spellings. Under an implementation that keeps only family names in the role definitions, `LA.ddflow_tools(role)` contains no flat `mcp__ddflow__ddflow_gate_*` entries, so `needed` is empty and the assertion passes, allowing the flat/core side of the “name both spellings” requirement to regress without failing this test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lean_agents.py:test_a_role_can_reach_what_its_work_needs_under_every_profile

chunk_findings.detail: The old test enforced that for `tier="all"` the recipe does **not** contain `"the core-tier config below"` or `"measured on the core tier"`. The new version deletes both negative checks and instead requires `"on the core tier"` to be present. Given a bad `WM.recipe(REL, tier="all")` output that says `"Use the core-tier config below:"`, the test would still pass as long as it also contains `"measured 10.7K for the researcher"` and `"on the core tier"`. The invariant the test is named for is no longer actually enforced.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_worker_mcp_config.py:test_the_recipe_does_not_call_the_configured_tier_core_when_it_is_not

chunk_findings.detail: The change only adds prose telling the agent it may use `ddflow_bug` action `found` on the lean profile; it does not add the family spellings to the role definitions’ tool allow-lists (the diff touching these files changes only this body line, with no `tools:` update anywhere in the manifest). Bug B07c4286c92 is that an `--agent ddflow-implementer` run with the default lean profile has no `ddflow_bug_found` or `ddflow_bug`/`ddflow_gate_*` tool exposed because the allow-list is flat-only. After this change, the prompt directs the agent to call `ddflow_bug` action `found`, but that tool is still not exposed, so the implementer facing the lean profile still cannot file a bug via the MCP tool; the bug remains unfixed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/claude_agents/ddflow-implementer.md:15 and ddflow-researcher.md:15

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `assert names <= core | {"ddflow_lesson_search"}` makes the `ddflow_lesson_search` requirement vacuous. `need["researcher"]` includes `ddflow_lesson_search`, but the asserted superset is `core | {"ddflow_lesson_search"}`, so the test still passes when `tier_tools("core")` omits that flat spelling. A regression that drops `mcp__ddflow__ddflow_lesson_search` from the core tier while leaving the other names would not fail this test, even though the test's own `need` says the researcher requires it; the assertion should compare `names` against `core` (or exclude `ddflow_lesson_search` explicitly only if it is not actually required from the core tier).
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lean_agents.py:test_the_flat_spellings_the_core_tier_lists_stay_allow_listed

chunk_findings.detail: `block = region.render(body, extra=_head_stamp(use_head))` stamps the kept front matter (`use_head`) rather than the template front matter (`head`). When `head_state == "edited"`, `use_head` is the operator’s hand-edited front matter, so the stamp records the operator’s edit as if ddflow wrote it. On the next adopt run where the template head changes again, `_refresh_head` sees `stamp.extra["head"] == content_digest(have)` and classifies the operator edit as ddflow’s own old front matter (`refresh`), so `_update_managed` silently replaces the hand-edited front matter even though it was supposed to be kept.
